title: 8C quiz with answer key
subject: Science
unit: Spring 2: The periodic table (8F); breathing and respiration (8C)
source: Seeded from science/y8 lesson 42 (8C quiz with answer key (portal))
intro: Covers lessons 25 to 42 of The periodic table (8F); breathing and respiration (8C). Answer every question. For multiple choice, fill in one circle.

questions.q: Which is a compound?
questions.a: B) H₂O. H₂O has two different elements chemically joined; O₂ and Fe are elements.

questions.q: Element D is shiny, conducts, and melts at -39 °C. It is...
questions.a: B) A metal (mercury). Shiny and conducting: metal. -39 °C fits mercury, the liquid metal.

questions.q: Carbon dioxide dissolves in water. The solution is...
questions.a: A) Acidic. Carbon dioxide is a non-metal oxide, so it is acidic.

questions.q: Why did gaps make the table convincing?
options: Predicted elements were later found with the predicted properties
questions.a: B) Predicted elements were later found with the predicted properties. Successful predictions are strong evidence for a scientific idea.

questions.q: Which element is in the same group as fluorine?
questions.a: B) Chlorine. Fluorine and chlorine are both Group 7 halogens.

questions.q: Potassium melts at 63 °C. Rubidium, below it, melts at about...
questions.a: B) 39 °C. Melting point decreases down Group 1, so it is lower than potassium.

questions.q: Which reacts most vigorously with water?
questions.a: C) Potassium. Reactivity increases down Group 1.

questions.q: Will bromine displace chlorine from sodium chloride?
questions.a: B) No. Bromine is less reactive than chlorine, so it cannot displace it.

questions.q: Which pair react: bromine + potassium iodide, or iodine + potassium bromide?
questions.a: A) Bromine + potassium iodide. Bromine is more reactive than iodine, so it displaces it.

questions.q: Where does aerobic respiration happen?
questions.a: B) Mitochondria in cells. In the mitochondria of every cell.

questions.q: Why are alveolus walls one cell thick?
questions.a: B) Short distance for diffusion. Thin walls mean gases diffuse quickly.

questions.q: Results 2.4, 2.6, 2.5 L. The mean is...
Why does a red blood cell have no nucleus?
questions.a: B) More space for haemoglobin. More haemoglobin means more oxygen carried.

questions.q: What do all gas exchange surfaces share?
options: Large surface area and thin surface
questions.a: B) Large surface area and thin surface. Large and thin surfaces make diffusion fast.

questions.q: Why do smokers often cough?
options: Cilia are damaged so mucus builds up
questions.a: A) Cilia are damaged so mucus builds up. Paralysed cilia cannot sweep mucus away, so the body coughs it up.

questions.q: Anaerobic respiration in muscles produces...
questions.a: B) Lactic acid. glucose → lactic acid in human muscles.

questions.q: Why did the hot bottle make little gas?
options: Yeast enzymes were damaged by heat
questions.a: A) Yeast enzymes were damaged by heat. High temperatures denature enzymes and kill yeast.

questions.q: Which organism uses spiracles?
questions.a: B) Insect. Insects take in air through spiracles.

questions.q: Which state has particles far apart and moving fast?
questions.a: Gas

questions.q: Is salt water a pure substance?
questions.a: No, it is a mixture
